mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly expansion in real GDP (GDPC1) above 2.0% annualized signals robust economic growth, which directly increases corporate earnings visibility and investor risk appetite, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth rate exceeds 2.0% annualized for two consecutive quarters yet S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of such cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 5.0% for three consecutive months, it indicates a completed tightening cycle where policy uncertainty has peaked, triggering a short-term equity rebound as markets price in stable monetary conditions over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains above 5.0% for 3 months but S&P 500 delivers negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% and drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 indicates stagflationary pressures where tight labor markets collide with supply constraints, compressing corporate margins and generating negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE < 3.5% and INDPRO < 100.0 occur but S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 signals manufacturing contraction ahead of a recession, causing equity sell-offs as earnings expectations reset downward over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100.0 during late-cycle expansion but S&P 500 delivers positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent annualized CPI inflation above 4.0% (CPIAUCSL) indicates entrenched price pressures that delay rate cuts, allowing corporate earnings to outpace discount rate increases and drive positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL remains above 4.0% annually for 3 months yet S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals labor market overheating that accelerates wage growth, prompting premature Fed tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE < 3.5% for 2 months but S&P 500 delivers positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in retail sales (RSAFS) above 0.5% monthly and CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 4.0% annually indicates demand-pull inflation that forces aggressive monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL > 4.0% annually occur but S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In post-recession recovery, a sustained unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% combined with nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200.0 thousand signals accelerating labor market strength that supports corporate hiring and earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE < 4.0 and PAYEMS > 200.0 occur during post-recession recovery but S&P 500 delivers negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances.
